The Q3 earnings cycle has brought several notable releases from the Magnificent 7 group, with Apple AAPL, Alphabet GOOGL, and Meta Platforms META all posting strong revenue growth and several impressive quarterly records.
Apple Posts Record Results  Apple delivered a strong fiscal Q4 release, with total revenue climbing 12% YoY to a September quarter record of $114.5 billion.
Earnings similarly reflected positivity, with EPS of $2.10 growing 14% from the same period last year.
The strong results helped Apple finish its fiscal year with record annual revenue of nearly $479 billion.
Alphabet Sees Explosive Cloud Growth  Alphabet's latest release was highlighted by explosive Google Cloud results, with segment revenue soaring 103% YoY to $30.7 billion.
Demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions continues to fuel the growth, with Cloud operating income also climbing significantly to $11.1 billion.
The broader business remained rock-solid as well, with total sales increasing 25% YoY to $127.6 billion.
Google Search revenue climbed 12%, with AI-related enhancements helping drive stronger search activity.
Meta's Advertising Momentum Remains Strong  Meta's core advertising business continues to shine, with total revenue climbing 26% YoY to $64.6 billion.
Ad impressions increased 10% from the same period last year, while the average price per ad jumped 14%.
Still, spending remains a major focus, with Meta forecasting $135-$145 billion in capital expenditures for 2026.

Baird Cut Its Qualcomm Target to $320.

It Still Sees 104% Upside ©@Golib via Canva, @sebastian-k from Getty Images via Canva   Key Takeaways   Baird cut its Qualcomm price target to $320 from $400 after the fiscal fourth-quarter report and kept its Outperform rating.
Baird's target implies 35x forward earnings, well above Qualcomm's five-year high of 26x, and fiscal 2027 estimates are still falling.
The fiscal 2029 plan may support Baird's optimism, but a year is too short for investors to pay for it in full while estimates fall.
Qualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) fell 9.49% to close at $156.75 on November 5, the day after its fiscal fourth-quarter report, as the PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped more than 10%.
That left the stock 38% below its May 29 closing high.
Baird cut its price target to $320 from $400 the same morning, and still sees 104% upside.
The memory shortage cut Android phone builds, costing more than $1.50 of fiscal 2026 EPS, management said in July.
Handset chip revenue fell 26% year over year to $5.1 billion in the September quarter, and Qualcomm expects another dip in December as Apple revenue shrinks.
Qualcomm is raising chip prices, with the full benefit due only in the second half of fiscal 2027.
It guided its chip unit's pre-tax margin to 20%-22% for December, down from 24% in September, though about 3 points of that comes from moving data center into the unit.
Automotive revenue hit a record $1.99 billion, up 89% year over year.
Data center sales start this quarter, as custom chips ship to Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) and a second hyperscaler, and management kept its $5 billion data center target for fiscal 2027.

Delphi Management's Founder Adds a Real Estate Leader While Trimming Cyclical Exposure  Scott Black (Trades, Portfolio) recently submitted his 13F filing for the third quarter of 2026, offering investors a window into the decisions made at Delphi Management, Inc., the Boston-based firm he founded and leads as president.

AAPL GF Value chart   Scott Black (Trades, Portfolio) is the president and founder of Delphi Management, Inc. His first entrepreneurial venture was restructuring the William O'Neil Company in 1978, followed in 1979 by managing equities for Sunkist Growers, Delphi Management's original account.

Black holds a BA from Johns Hopkins University in Applied Mathematics and Economics and earned an MBA in Finance at the Harvard Business School in 1971, after completing his U.S. Army active service obligation at Fort Ord, California.

Summary of New Buys  Scott Black (Trades, Portfolio) added a total of 2 stocks, among them:   The most significant addition was Simon Property Group Inc (NYSE:SPG), with 6,020 shares, accounting for 1.27% of the portfolio and a total value of $1.21 million.

The second largest addition to the portfolio was Allison Transmission Holdings Inc (NYSE:ALSN), consisting of 1,795 shares, representing approximately 0.21% of the portfolio, with a total value of $200,000.
